relevance_note: Case series of three Chinese HA20 pedigrees with TNFAIP3 carriers described individually: "we report eight patients with HA20 from three unrelated families in China".
method_note:
Read the whole paper; built the JSON with a Python script in the scratch directory. All values come from my reading. The script copied Table 1 rows from the paper file to build row-segment spans; I checked every table-derived value against Table 1 by eye. All spans checked verbatim by script.
TABLE 1 MAPPING: Table 1 has no patient-label column (first column = pedigree number). Rows were matched by pedigree, sex and ages: row 1 = P1 (F, onset 18, diagnosis 28); rows 2-4 = IV:14, V:22, V:26 (the three are identical, so the order does not matter); row 5 = IV:1 (Family 2) (onset 9, diagnosis 12); row 6 = P2 (onset 15, diagnosis 35); row 7 = P3 (M); row 8 = IV:1 (Family 3) (onset 8, diagnosis 10). The legend defines '-, negative' and '+, postive'; the table prints an en dash, treated as the defined negative symbol, with the legend quoted as a second span. 'UN, unknown' = not reported.
LABELS: probands use the paper's own P1/P2/P3 (pedigree IDs V:24, III:5, III:3 also printed). 'IV:1' is used in Families 2 and 3 and 'III:3' in Families 1-3, so the daughters are 'IV:1 (Family 2)' and 'IV:1 (Family 3)' and the Family 2 cousin is 'III:3 (Family 2)'. Relatives use their pedigree IDs.
SCOPE: 14 people: 8 TNFAIP3 carriers (P1, IV:14, V:22, V:26, P2, IV:1 (Family 2), P3, IV:1 (Family 3)) and 6 relatives described in relation to them: IV:13 (P1's father, 'had no symptoms'; the NOD2 variant is called 'paternal' but his genotype is not stated, so he has no variant row), II:3, III:3 (Family 2), III:4 (affected; 'refused to do the gene testing'), II:4 and I:4 (affected; no testing reported). Left out: III:2 and III:3 of Family 1 (only 'were cousins'), cousin V:10 and VI:7 (G6PD deficiency only, not HA20, no TNFAIP3 testing). The literature review (126 patients, 35 articles) is reported only in aggregate, with no individual-level detail, so it gives no rows.
CONTRADICTIONS IN THE PAPER: (1) P1 genital ulcers: text 'recurrent oral and genital ulcers' and Discussion 'oral and genital ulcers', but Table 1 '-'; both rows emitted, checklist not reported. (2) P2 fever: text 'without recurrent fever', Table 1 '+'; both rows, checklist not reported. (3) IV:1 (Family 2) fever: text 'recurrent fever', Table 1 '-'; both rows, checklist not reported. (4) P3 age at onset: text 'recurrent oral ulcers since the age of 10', Table 1 onset '15'; recorded the text value. (5) P3 autoantibodies: positive anti-TG and anti-TPO (text and Table 1) vs 'Blood tests for CBC, biochemistry panel, and autoantibodies were all normal'; both rows, checklist not reported. (6) P3: 'Henoch-Schonlein purpura at age 30' vs Table 1 skin lesions '-'; both rows, checklist skin lesions not reported; vasculitis marked observed on the basis of HSP. (7) A547T: Abstract 'validated to be pathogenic in our study' vs Discussion 'the accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown'; both quoted in pathogenicity. Also P1: Table 1 and Discussion say arthritis, the text says 'joint pain ... without joint swelling'; recorded arthralgia observed, arthritis observed (table), joint swelling excluded.
OTHER CHOICES: Probands' text ages (28, 35, 40) equal the Table 1 age at diagnosis, so they are recorded only as age at diagnosis; the daughters' '13-year-old' and '10-year-old' (pedigree descriptions) are recorded as age at last evaluation. Consanguinity: 'the proband's grandmother (III:2) and maternal grandfather (III:3) were cousins' does not say whose parents they are, so not reported for everyone. Zygosity of A547T in IV:14, V:22 and V:26 is not stated per person (not reported); the sisters' inheritance is 'inherited maternal' because the proband's mother is stated to carry the variant (assumes full sisters). Transcript NM_006290.4 is printed in the text for A547T only; Table 1's header 'NM_006290' is used for the other TNFAIP3 rows. R271X variant class is not stated by the authors (not reported). P2's anemia has no stated cause, so 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is not reported; a normal CBC (P1, P3) is recorded as excluded. Narrow negatives (no arthritis, no uveitis, no follicles, no abdominal pain) do not exclude the composite checklist items. IV:1 (Family 3) ocular item excluded from 'without gastrointestinal or ocular symptoms' plus Table 1 uveitis '-'. Group statements naming each relative (e.g. 'Her mother (IV:14) and her two sisters (V:22, V:26) had ...') are treated as stated for each individual. Post-treatment statements (e.g. P1 'did not exhibit fever, arthralgia, oral ulcers, or eye discomfort after a year of treatment') are not used as exclusions. The father's 'no symptoms' is recorded as one excluded feature; no checklist item excluded from it. Functional evidence for c.1906+2T>G was measured in P2's cells and is repeated on the daughter's row because it describes the variant; A547T had only an in silico structure model. HLA-B27, TB-SPOT, biochemistry, urine, Ig and complement results were not recorded as features. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (the paper does not say).
